facts.summary: wiki_execute_command is declared as a public C API in include/wiki_demo_api.h:12 (with extern "C" guard). Its parameter `const char *command` is directly caller-controlled — any external caller can pass an arbitrary string. The function is non-static (confirmed by snapshot is_static=false). Per validation requirements, zero repository callers is expected for header-declared entries and is not dead-code evidence.

The caller-controlled `command` parameter flows directly to system(command) at src/command_runner.c:10 with no sanitization. The only guard (line 6) checks command==NULL || command[0]=='\0', which only rejects NULL and empty strings. Any non-empty string — including malicious shell metacharacters — passes through unchanged to system(). Call graph confirms system is the sole callee.

The guard at line 6 (if command==NULL || command[0]=='\0') is insufficient for command injection. It only rejects NULL and empty-string inputs. It does not sanitize shell metacharacters, validate against an allowlist, or use a safe exec-family alternative. Any non-empty attacker-crafted string (e.g., "ls; rm -rf /") passes the guard and reaches system() at line 10.
